script.title: Why the Leaning Tower of Pisa Is Also Curved
sentences: The tower was only two floors high when it started sinking.
This was Pisa in 1178, and its three-metre foundation sat in weak, unstable soil.
Then construction stopped for the better part of a century.
When work resumed, engineers built the upper floors taller on one side to make up for the tilt.
So the tower is actually curved.
The job took 199 years in all.
That long pause happened because Pisa was almost always at war with Genoa, Lucca and Florence, and it let the soil settle.
Without it, the tower would almost certainly have toppled.
scenes: Extreme close-up of a worried medieval Pisan master mason's weathered face in 1178, wide eyes staring upward at a white marble wall tilting above him, dust in the air, harsh afternoon sun.

Medieval workers in tunics at Pisa in 1178 digging a shallow foundation into soft, wet, muddy ground beside a cathedral, the half-built two-storey white marble tower beginning to lean, overcast light, wide shot.
The abandoned two-storey leaning white marble stump of the Pisa tower overgrown with weeds and wooden scaffolding rotting, a lone shepherd with goats passing, quiet golden evening light, wide shot.

Medieval Italian engineers in robes measuring with plumb lines and wooden rulers on a high scaffold, carefully stacking marble blocks taller on one side, focused expressions, bright midday light, medium shot.
The Leaning Tower of Pisa in white marble seen in profile against a clear blue sky, its upper floors visibly curving back like a gentle banana shape, low-angle dramatic view, crisp daylight.
Generations of medieval masons at work on the Pisa tower, scaffolds and wooden cranes on its upper galleries, the bell chamber being completed, warm sunset light, wide establishing shot.

Medieval Pisan soldiers in chainmail marching past the unfinished leaning tower toward war galleys on the river, banners flying, the tower quietly standing behind them, stormy dramatic sky, wide shot.
The Leaning Tower of Pisa standing defiantly at a steep tilt on a green lawn beside the cathedral, golden sunrise light, low-angle heroic composition, slight mist around its base.
script.description:
The Leaning Tower of Pisa began to sink in 1178.
A century-long pause is the reason it is still standing.
visuals: Leaning Tower of Pisa close up arcades
claims_en: In 1178 the tower began to sink after construction progressed to the second floor.
The tower had a three-metre foundation set in weak, unstable subsoil.
Construction was halted for the better part of a century.
To compensate for the tilt, engineers built upper floors with one side taller than the other.
Because of this, the tower is curved.
Construction occurred in three stages over 199 years.
Construction was halted because the Republic of Pisa was almost continually engaged in battles with Genoa, Lucca and Florence.
The halt allowed time for the underlying soil to settle.
Otherwise, the tower would almost certainly have toppled.
